title: Microwave doors: what explains metal mesh?

lines: Look closely at a microwave door: there's a metal mesh.
It is not decoration. It is part of the shield.
Inside, a device called a magnetron produces the microwaves.
The oven works as a Faraday cage that keeps the energy inside.
The holes in the mesh are much smaller than the wavelength of the microwaves.
So the microwaves cannot pass through the door.
Visible light has a far shorter wavelength, so it passes straight through.
That is why you can watch your food while the energy stays in.

traceability.purpose: Hook: frame 0 is the oven with its lit window; as the line names the mesh, a loupe opens on the door and the holes in the metal mesh become visible.

evidence.claim: The perforations in the mesh are much smaller than the microwaves' wavelength, so microwave radiation cannot pass through the door while visible light can.
evidence.quote: Because the size of the perforations in the mesh is much less than the microwaves' wavelength (12.2 cm for the usual 2.45 GHz), microwave radiation cannot pass through the door, while visible light (with its much shorter wavelength) can.

evidence.claim: The door of a microwave oven usually has a window with a layer of conductive mesh to maintain the shielding.
evidence.quote: The oven door usually has a window for easy viewing, with a layer of conductive mesh some distance from the outer panel to maintain the shielding.

evidence.claim: A microwave oven uses a Faraday cage, partly visible covering the window, to contain the electromagnetic energy within the oven.
evidence.quote: A microwave oven uses a partial Faraday shield (on five of its interior six sides) and a partial Faraday cage, consisting of a wire mesh, on the sixth side (the transparent window), to contain the electromagnetic energy within the oven and to protect the user from exposure to microwave radiation.

traceability.purpose: Shield: not decoration: the metal body and the mesh light up together as one continuous shield around the cavity.

evidence.claim: The door of a microwave oven usually has a window with a layer of conductive mesh to maintain the shielding.

traceability.purpose: Source: the oven in cutaway; as the line names it, the magnetron in the corner starts launching microwaves into the metal box.

evidence.claim: Microwaves are produced inside the oven by an electron tube called a magnetron.
evidence.quote: A device called a magnetron inside the oven produces microwaves.
evidence.source: Microwave Ovens | FDA (fetched 2026-10-28T09:27:13.688Z, text sha256 ede428dc4d146722)

evidence.claim: A federal standard limits the amount of microwaves that can leak from an oven throughout its lifetime to 5 milliwatts of microwave radiation per square centimeter at approximately 2 inches from the oven surface.
evidence.quote: A Federal standard (21 CFR 1030.10) limits the amount of microwaves that can leak from an oven throughout its lifetime to 5 milliwatts (mW) of microwave radiation per square centimeter at approximately 2 inches from the oven surface.
evidence.source: Microwave Ovens | FDA (fetched 2026-10-28T09:27:13.688Z, text sha256 ede428dc4d146722)
